goal: Collect knowledge about how to work out what a text says, and connect the pieces you collected.

observations.text: A claim is checkable only if it carries the exact offsets of the passage it was taken from. Without them a reader cannot return to the source.
Checking that a quoted span occurs in the document verifies provenance and not truth. The check has no operation that can mark a claim true.
The share of a document that admitted claims anchor to is a warning light and not a score. It moves with how the contract defines a claim.
A passage no claim reaches is a question for the reader and not a defect. It may be a heading, a transition, or prose that carries no claim.
Extraction gets worse as a document grows longer, while a deterministic check over the same document does not. The two halves do not scale alike.
An anchor that reaches into the text of two speakers merges two positions into one node. The anchor is the only record of who said it.
A rule can settle whether two strings share a passage. It cannot settle what a passage means, and it damages a judgement when it is allowed to try.
An extractor that always answers is worse than one that abstains outside a closed set of kinds. Anything else is intentionally ignored.
